test_title: RRB Technician Grade III Official Paper (Held On: 20 Dec, 2024 Shift 2)
subject: general
question: What is the speed v of an athlete, if the athlete takes t seconds to go once around a circular path of radius r ?
solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

For any **circular motion**, the total **distance** covered in one complete lap is the **circumference** of the circle.

**Circumference** = 2πr

**Speed (v)** = Distance ÷ Time = 2πr / t

**∴ The correct answer is v = 2πr/t.**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/33243a56dc11cefc11b239680669d9857699659e5d3b26dfe187bb88c2086f64.png] 

**Given:**

Radius of the circular path = **r**

Time taken for one revolution = **t**

**Formula Used:**

**Speed (v)** = Total Distance / Total Time

**Calculations:**

⇒ Distance covered in one round = **Circumference of the circle**

⇒ Distance = 2 × π × r = 2πr

⇒ Speed (v) = Distance / Time

⇒ v = 2πr / t

**∴ The correct answer is v = 2πr/t.**

**__Additional Information__**

Uniform Circular Motion

When an object moves in a circular path with **constant speed**, its motion is called uniform circular motion. Even if speed is constant, **velocity** changes due to direction change.

Angular Velocity (ω)

The rate of change of **angular displacement**. Relation with linear speed is **v = rω**, where ω = 2π/t.

Displacement vs Distance

After one full revolution, the **displacement** is 0 (since the athlete returns to the start), but the **distance** is the full circumference 2πr.</p
